title: Runtime release QA and signoff contract
author: Jordan Liu
content:
Summary:
This document defines the cross-functional QA and signoff contract for runtime releases (minor and major) across Redwood Inference. It consolidates acceptance gates that must be satisfied before a release is certified for canary and progressive rollout. The contract covers (1) performance and cost regression checks, (2) kernel scheduling safety checks, (3) profiling and tracing artefacts required, (4) benchmark reproducibility criteria, (5) release signoff matrix and owners, and (6) a lightweight post-release monitoring runbook.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce risk of runtime releases by giving a clear, repeatable QA checklist tied to measurable signals and named owners.
- Scope: Applies to release candidates for the serving runtime and scheduler components that touch kernel selection, batching, KV cache behavior, or scheduling policies. Does NOT cover UI console changes or separate control-plane-only releases unless they change routing or fallback behaviour.

Prerelease gating overview (quick list):
1) Unit + integration test pass (CI) with no flaky tests > 2% on last 48h runs.
2) Benchmark sanity: end-to-end synthetic throughput and p95 latency within thresholds (see metrics below).
3) Kernel scheduling safety checks passed (collision, priority inversion, graceful preemption).
4) Profiling evidence collected for representative workloads and uploaded to Profiling DB (links + tags present).
5) Release notes drafted and reviewers assigned.
6) Product and SRE signoffs recorded in the signoff matrix.

Metrics and acceptance thresholds (must be provided with every RC):
- Baseline: Use the baseline named in the release ticket (format: baseline/<release>-<date>).
- SLO coverage: Must not worsen tail latency (p99) by more than 10% compared to baseline on the same synthetic corpus under identical load-shaping.
- Cost-per-1k-tokens: No increase > 7% for the median token cost in the target workload.
- Throughput: Sustained throughput (tokens/s) drop must be < 8% for mixed small/long sequences.
- KV cache hit rate: Must be within +/- 2 percentage points of baseline for workloads that exercise caching.
- Regression budget: A release may exceed one threshold by up to the tolerance above only with explicit SRE approval and a mitigation plan.

Benchmarking and reproducibility checklist:
- Bench harness: Use the release harness image: registry.redwood/release-harness:<rc-tag>.
- Command skeleton (example):
  ./bench/run-suite.sh --corpus=release/corpora/<name> --rc=<rc-tag> --baseline=<baseline-tag> --reruns=3 --trace-output=traces/<rc-tag>.tar.gz
- Required artifacts to attach to the release ticket: raw traces (tar.gz), aggregated metrics csv, kernel-hint logs, and the harness command used.
- Reproducibility pass: At least two independent runs on separate nodes must produce metrics within 4% variance for p50/p95/p99. If variance is > 4%, capture environment diff and escalate to release lead.

Profiling and tracing evidence (mandatory):
- Required profiles: kernel latency histograms, GPU occupancy timeline, scheduler decision traces, and request-level end-to-end traces correlated to kernel calls.
- Sampling policy: For release QA, use stratified sampling: 30% tail-heavy (high-entropy inputs), 50% mixed workload, 20% long-sequence stress.
- Artefact naming convention: profiling/<rc-tag>/<workload>-<sample-type>-<timestamp>.tar.gz
- Upload: All profiling artefacts must be uploaded to Profiling DB and linked on the release ticket. Missing uploads block signoff.

Kernel scheduling safety checks (checklist):
- Preflight static checks: verify kernel compatibility matrix for new kernels; ensure no kernel drops required ops for primary model families.
- Priority sanity: Run priority-inversion unit checks against the priority simulator with the new policy flag. Command:
  tooling/priority-sim --policy=policies/<rc-policy>.yaml --inject=priority-inversion.yaml
- Preemption test: Validate cooperative preemption works end-to-end on the staging pool; confirm that long-running batches can be preempted and resumed without state corruption.
- Admission controller: Validate decline/circuit behavior under overload by replaying synthetic spike profile (tooling/loadgen --spike-file spikes/short-burst.json).
- Kernel fallback: Execute canary fallback script to force kernel fallback and confirm request correctness and bounded latency increase.

Known-issues and risk catalog (what to check explicitly):
- NVLink transient degradation: If the RC touches memory packaging, include the nvlink health probe in the bench run.
- KV cache warmup regression: Ensure warmup trace shows expected hit-rate ramp profiles.
- Quantization boundary behaviours: If new quant kernels are present, run the quant-sanity corpus and check output deltas against float baseline (tolerance set in the ticket).
- Multi-tenant noise: For changes touching admission or scheduler, run multi-tenant noise-injection bench (noise/mt-noise.json).

Release signoff matrix (table as plain text):
- Release owner: <engineer who opened RC> (required)
- Release lead (engineering): name, email
- SRE approver: name, email
- Product approver: name, email (if behavior changes user-visible latency/cost)
- Security: name, email (required only if RC touches crypto/keys/networking)
- Observability: name, email
- Signoff fields (each must be present on ticket): approvals: [engineering, sre, product (if applicable), observability], bench artifacts link, profiling artifacts link, rollout plan link.

Signoff timeline and rules:
1) RC must be in the staging channel for a minimum of 48 hours before canary, during which the bench and profiling runs occur.
2) Emergency opt-outs: If a blocker is discovered after signoff but before canary, the release owner must create an emergency rollback plan and notify the SRE pager.
3) Conditional signoffs: A partial signoff (engineering + SRE only) can permit a limited canary of up to 2% capacity for high-confidence fixes; product signoff remains required for broader rollouts.

Canary and rollout plan (minimum required content):
- Canary size and duration: default 2% of production capacity for 6 hours with 1h ramp. Adjust only with SRE approval.
- Canary metrics to monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (5xx), kernel fallback events, KV cache hit-rate, GPU thermal events, and cost-per-token trend.
- Automatic abort criteria (examples): p99 > baseline * 1.15 for 10m sustained, error-rate increase > 2x baseline for 5m, kernel fallback rate > 0.5% sustained for 15m.

Post-release monitoring and quick recovery steps:
1) Monitor the Canary dashboard (link template: dashboards/release/<rc-tag>).
2) If abort criteria triggered, pause rollout, move traffic back to previous variant, and initiate rollback runbook.
3) If subtle regressions (cost or small latency blips) appear, open a P1 ticket and tag the release owner and SRE.

Example rollback checklist (short):
- Step 1: Pause the rollout and divert traffic to baseline route: CLI example:
  rctl route switch --from=release/<rc-tag> --to=baseline/<baseline-tag> --immediate
- Step 2: Scale down RC instances by 50% while keeping control plane alive for diagnostics.
- Step 3: Collect and attach artifacts (logs, traces, kernel metrics) to incident ticket.

Ownership and contacts (examples):
- Release lead: Jordan Liu (jordan@redwood.ai)
- SRE lead: Sofia Martinez (sofia@redwood.ai)
- Observability owner: Ethan Green (ethan@redwood.ai)
- Product representative: Priya Patel (priya@redwood.ai)

Appendix A — Common CLI snippets and JSON templates:
- Bench run example (full):
  ./bench/run-suite.sh --corpus=release/corpora/mixed-sample-2024 --rc=rc-2024-09-18 --baseline=baseline-2024-08-05 --reruns=3 --trace-output=artifacts/rc-2024-09-18-traces.tar.gz

- Priority policy minimal JSON (example):
  {
    "policy_name": "slo-driven-default",
    "priorities": ["realtime", "interactive", "background"],
    "preemption": {"enabled": true, "grace_window_ms": 120}
  }

- Profiling upload command (example):
  tooling/profile-uploader --input=profiling/rc-2024-09-18.tar.gz --rc=rc-2024-09-18 --tags=release,rc

Document maintenance and review cadence:
- This contract is reviewed quarterly by the Release Council (engineering + SRE + product).
- Any deviation for a particular RC must be recorded on the release ticket and explicitly approved by the SRE approver.

Appendix B — Short decision log (changes vs prior process):
- 2024-09-18: Initial contract authored (Jordan Liu).
- 2024-11-04: Added fixed reproducibility variance threshold (4%).
- 2025-02-14: Tightened cost regression threshold from 10% to 7% after Q4 incidents.

If you are preparing an RC and need help executing any of the checks above, tag @release-support in Slack or create a small office-hours request with SRE for live assistance.
